reader.requirement: On a tie for the least value FUNCTION MIN returns the content of the leftmost argument-1 having that value, for every argument class COBOL-85 allows (numeric, integer, alphanumeric, alphabetic mixed with alphanumeric).

native vs standard-decimal arithmetic arm (num.StandardDecimal); COBOL-85 has no ARITHMETIC clause so it always takes the native arm, the same arm a 2023 program without ARITHMETIC takes

reader.notes: ExtremeIndex updates the selection only on a strictly smaller argument, so the leftmost of equal values is kept; the string carrier compares with space padding (CobolString.Compare) or the PCS. Same output at --std 2023. Observation (not a conformance defect): CobolIntrinsics.ExactValue.cs#SelectExact re-writes the leftmost-strict-update loop beside the unified ExtremeIndex kernel (PB2635 unified the other carriers); the exact lane is what native ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN/MAX/MIN take.
